items.mnemonic: Look through the FRAME: ONE bar across the top, a MOUTH below. Every mask pressed through this FRAME comes out with the exact SAME face.
ONE MOUTH gives the order, a BROOM sweeps the floor, and a HOOK on the wall holds the to-do list: another small MATTER handled before lunch.
Point at your own NOSE, the way people here do when they mean 'me': that gesture is SELF.
Dawn at the TENT: TWO LEGS stretch out of the flap, the camper shoulders a pack, and off down the trail — this is how a journey will DEPART.
An OLD man dozes in the SUN on the station bench. Ask who left the umbrella and every finger points at him: SOMEONE.
Turn over a spade of EARTH and a SCORPION scuttles out — the oldest tenant of any patch of GROUND.
A VOCATION is the work you were cut out for; practice it every day at the same counter and it becomes your BUSINESS.
A weathered signpost with a single arm at the crossroads: it tells you nothing but a DIRECTION.
On the packed EARTH the SUN rises over ONE FLAG planted for the festival; that is where the whole town gathers, so it is the PLACE.
Every MOUTH in the office is fed from the same SHELL of money, the company purse; each of those mouths is a MEMBER.
At the GATE a bar of ONE heavy beam is lifted by TWO HANDS, and the doors swing wide: OPEN.
A flexed arm with the bicep bulging and the elbow hooked down: pure POWER.
You stand at the GATE and a MOUTH calls through the gap, 'Who is it?' — the first QUESTION of every visit.
A PERSON pulls up the STAKE that marks his plot and hands it to a newcomer who will farm it in his place: a SUBSTITUTE.
SUN and MOON hang side by side in one sky — twice the light, so everything below is BRIGHT.
A THOUSAND hands in the VILLAGE put their POWER behind the festival float, and the great heavy thing begins to MOVE.
Under a tall LID of roof sits a MOUTH-shaped hall, and SMALL houses spread out at its feet: the CAPITAL.
On the ROAD a crow's BEAK pecks at the handcart we UTILIZE every morning; this is the lane the cart is allowed to PASS THROUGH.
The KING walks the VILLAGE lanes, hears each dispute, and settles every one by REASON.
A PERSON hugs a BOOK to the chest — an anatomy text, every page about the BODY.
Four plots divided by low mud walls, seen from the hill path above: a RICE FIELD.
A DROP of flame burns in the lamp above the KING's chair; whoever keeps that flame lit is the MASTER.
At SUN-up ONE guard calls STOP and asks the traveler at the HEAD of the line what the day's TOPIC is before anyone passes.
A SOUND rises straight from the HEART before any words are ready: an IDEA.
A bird beating its wings against a ceiling it cannot pass — the NEGATIVE sign, a flat NOT.
A PERSON picks up a SAW, and from a single plank begins to MAKE a shelf.
A fence of rails you UTILIZE as a gate, a ladder, a bench — whatever the job, the thing is in USE.
Under the LEAN-TO, TWENTY notches are cut into a post, and a RIGHT HAND measures how far the shadow has crept: one more DEGREE.
A BOW kept PRIVATE in its case, and an INSECT, the beetle that lifts a hundred times its own weight: both are STRONG.
EIGHT openings cut in the fence, so nothing behind it stays PRIVATE: the garden is now PUBLIC.
A HAND at the TEMPLE gate closes around the offering box and will not let go: HOLD.
Past the last VILLAGE house a crow's BEAK pecks at the stubble where the paths FINISH: the open FIELD.
A cord tied to a plow and a person pulling it — the WHEREBY, the tool by which a thing gets done: BY MEANS OF.
A RICE FIELD drawn above a HEART: the farmer's chest is full of next spring's planting, and that is how you THINK.
A ROOF with a PIG snoring underneath it — the old farmyard picture of a HOUSE.
Three tens bound together make thirty years, one GENERATION; live through three of them and you have watched the whole WORLD change.
Draw ONE line and STOP exactly on it, not a hair further: that is CORRECT.
On the HILL a wide ROOF shelters TWO pairs of LEGS pacing the corridor in white coats: an INSTITUTION.
Three drops of blood around a curved valve — the pump itself, the HEART.
Drive a WEDGE down between two plots of RICE FIELD and you have drawn a BOUNDARY.
An OLD teacher sits beside a CHILD while each STRIKE of the pointer taps the slate — this is how you TEACH.
Crossed lines inked on a collar, humanity's first deliberate pattern: WRITING.
TWO strokes for a head and LEGS underneath: a figure standing at the start line, the ORIGIN.
A THOUSAND sacks of rice stacked in one VILLAGE storehouse until the floor groans: HEAVY.
On the ROAD you hear an AXE chopping just beyond the bend — the woodcutter's hut must be NEAR.
An OLD scholar leans on a HOOK-shaped cane, chin on the handle, letting the question turn slowly: CONSIDER.
ONE line across the top, a RICE FIELD in the middle, the whole thing set in a CONTAINER like a frame on the wall: a PICTURE.
WATER wide enough to hold every PERSON alive, the MOTHER that every river runs home to: the SEA.
A SAMURAI pulls the COVER off his cart and his LEGS carry him through the market calling out prices: SELL.
A question flies like an ARROW and the MOUTH answers before it lands: KNOW.
One SMALL BIRD lands in the TREE at dusk, then a dozen more follow until the branches chatter — they GATHER.
A MOUTH calls goodbye from the deck, POWER hauls on the ropes, and a SWORD cuts the last mooring line: the boats SEPARATE.
A COW at the market with a little FLAG pinned to its flank, tagged and priced like any other item for sale: a THING.
A PERSON holds ONE brush by the MIDDLE and makes a single STROKE across the order form: the tool you USE.
MOUTH, MOUTH, MOUTH — three open boxes stacked on a shop shelf, each holding a different item: GOODS.
SAY the numbers aloud up to TEN on your fingers, then start again from one: that is how you MEASURE.
A BONE lies beside a SPOON on the cleared table; the meal is over, and so is the long life it fed: DEATH.
A COW kept at the TEMPLE, garlanded with flowers and never once put to the plow: SPECIAL.
A farmer tucks his GRAIN into a PRIVATE jar, and on the lid he writes one word: I.
A WOMAN whispers a PRIVATE word to herself, then opens her MOUTH to the whole room — this is how the story will BEGIN.
TEN rays above the SUN, TEN below it in the grass, and the pale MOON still hanging at the edge of the sky: MORNING.
Down the ROAD rolls a CAR with a tarp COVER lashed over its load of crates: CARRY.
The THREAD runs off the spool, the WALKING LEGS slow on the ICE of the year's last month, and the road reaches its END.
A PRIVATE citizen climbs onto a crate, and the MOUTH above it addresses the whole square: the raised PLATFORM.
A LEAN-TO roof with only one PRIVATE little mark on the floor beneath it and nothing else at all: the space is WIDE.
A PERSON keeps a DROP of oil burning in the KING's lamp at the same doorway every night: this is where they LIVE.
A rack of forty candles burned down to NOTHINGNESS, not one flame left standing: NOTHING.
TEN witnesses, each with an EYE on the object, ONE verdict, EIGHT signatures at the bottom: TRUE.
An ARM reaches up and the fingers close around the MOON itself — now you HAVE it.
A RICE FIELD with a NAIL driven in at its corner to mark where the first lane will run: the beginning of a TOWN.
RICE measured out by the LADLE at the counter, scoop by scoop, and paid for by the scoop: the FEE.
A carpenter's square: two bars joined by one upright, the oldest mark of CRAFT.
A BRUSH draws the plan while the long STRETCH of the stroke beneath it lays out the foundation line: BUILD.
Through a HOLE in the roof, all the builder's CRAFT shows you is the blue SKY.
Hair BOUND UP, BROOM in hand, HEART racing — the guests arrive in five minutes, so HURRY.
A footprint with the toes pointing up, planted hard on the line: STOP.
Down the ROAD goes a parcel with little HORNS of ribbon on top, lifted toward HEAVEN by the courier's raised hands: SEND.
SEVEN quick slices with one SWORD across the melon on the board: CUT.
A CAR hits a patch of CLOUD-grey ice on the pass and its wheels begin to ROLL.
A flat STONE, ONE blade, and TWO HANDS working it back and forth until the edge shines: POLISH.
Drop into the HOLE and climb down NINE levels, deeper than anyone has gone before: INVESTIGATE.
A WHITE drum with HORNS of tassels hangs from a TREE stand in the shrine yard; strike it and out comes MUSIC.
You RUN from the futon the instant a SNAKE slides across the tatami — nothing makes you WAKE UP faster.
A SHEEP's wool pulled down over your EYE like a hood against the wind: something you WEAR.
Under the SICKNESS roof, ONE bed inside a wooden FRAME holds a PERSON who cannot get up today: ILLNESS.
AXE and AXE, two blades tapped against a SHELL coin on the block to hear whether it rings true: QUALITY.
One STEP inside the TEMPLE gate you fold your hands, stand still, and WAIT.
SAY what you will do, drive the STAKE into the ground, and show your CRAFT in front of the judges: this is the TEST.
Under one banner pointing a single DIRECTION, a PERSON passes an ARROW to the next in line, and so on down the generations: a TRIBE.
GOLD that stays STUBBORN and pale, refusing to turn yellow no matter how long it sits in the fire: SILVER.
The SUN is only TEN steps up the sky, balanced on a post: it is still EARLY.
The SUN throws a BIG image onto the white sheet stretched in a FRAME: REFLECT.
To STAND in the TREE at the end of the lane and SEE the children all the way home: a PARENT.
Before buying the HORSE you run an AWL along its hoof to check that the horn is sound: VERIFY.
In the GRASS stands a FRAME holding one BIG bloom brighter than all the rest; that brilliance was borrowed to spell the name of ENGLISH.
A BOX with a single ARROW laid inside it — the healer's old field kit, the start of MEDICINE.
A PERSON stands at the SAMURAI's elbow, ready to fetch, carry and SERVE.
Heap EARTH over your PRIVATE things in the yard, shoulder the pack, and walk off down the road: LEAVE.
The MOUTH says 'NOT YET' — one more second on the tongue before it decides on the TASTE.
A COVER slides down over the page, and the inked stone beneath will BESTOW its image on the paper: a COPY.
